key_insight: A hybrid SCAPS-1D and machine-learning workflow identified an optimized CdSnP2-based integrated solar cell-photodetector design that substantially boosts both power conversion and photoresponse.
engineering_relevance: The study provides a data-driven route to tune layer thickness, doping, and defects for multifunctional optoelectronic devices with faster design cycles and clearer process targets.
method: Generated SCAPS-1D simulation data across 13 device architectures and multiple layer parameters.
Trained six machine-learning models plus one deep-learning model to predict device performance.
Used SHAP analysis to explain which interfaces and material properties most strongly control outcomes.
evidence_signal: The best configuration, n-CdS/p-CdSnP2/p+-CGS with a 200 nm CGS BSF layer, improved efficiency from 20.67% to 32.69%, responsivity from 0.53 to 0.72 A/W, and detectivity from 2.51×10^14 to 1.78×10^16 Jones.
watch_item: The optimization is simulation- and model-driven, so experimental fabrication, interface quality, and material stability still need validation.
paper_title: Machine learning-assisted design and explainable optimization of CdSnP2-based integrated solar-photodetector devices
